name: Coinbase Premium Drift
description: Tested whether a widening Coinbase premium over Binance (US buyers working orders on USD venues) predicts the next 15-minute move, which Kalshi's opening price ignores. It does, consistently but weakly: about 51-55% right in the strongest tenth of cases, not enough to beat the fee and spread.
hypothesis: US flow is worked on USD venues (Coinbase) over hours; while it's working, Coinbase trades at a premium/discount to Binance USDT and the global price keeps drifting that way. A widening premium should predict the next 15-min return in its direction; Kalshi opens each window at ~50/50. Wrong if corr(premium change, next return) isn't positive in both halves on two coins, or the top-decile hit rate is too low to beat a taker's fee + spread at the open (~53-54%).
next: Rejected at research: right sign everywhere (corr +0.02..+0.036) but too weak (top-decile hit 51-55%, ~+2c gross vs ~3c costs). Could be one input to a combined model; live use would also need a USDT feed recorded.
